findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: punctuality-linked quality payments in transport franchises are standardly defined as the share of services arriving within a contractual tolerance window, which is option C verbatim.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: option A stacks three absolutizers ('only', 'every', 'exactly on schedule') and is eliminable without the passage - no real performance regime pays on perfection.
justification: Eliminated A on form, then domain knowledge of how performance payments are written picks C over B and D. C is also the only option that makes the rest of the unit cohere: q5/D advertises 'a rising reliability figure', which only becomes a quarrel if the payment turns on a margin a lengthened timetable can widen. I could not infer the size of the margin, the value of the payment, or whether the operator earned it. Note the student-available lever is only A's absolutizer (4->3); the rest is specialist knowledge.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: option B's 'Every sailing that year' is an absolutizer, eliminable blind.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: q4/A fixes Cottam as the operator's defender, and the canonical defence of a lengthened timetable is that the old one understated the real crossing time (A). Option C ('broadly realistic') would destroy that defence, so it is incoherent in Cottam's mouth.
justification: Got to A vs D by eliminating B on form and C on argumentative role. A and D are both operator-friendly lines and I cannot separate them from the stems alone - D is a weaker version of the same defence. About 60% on A: above chance, not decisive. I could not infer the actual crossing time, the printed time, or what evidence Cottam offers.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: option C ('Nothing that has happened ... can be blamed') is an absolutizing exculpation; option B inverts cause and intent (no company withdraws a boat in order to lengthen gaps between sailings), so it reads as a manufactured distractor.

ENTAILMENT: the stem asks what is 'implied', and D is the only option shaped as an inference - a comparative magnitude claim ('more departures ... than the timetable changes had') rather than a bare fact.
justification: Reached D by eliminating C on form, B on causal incoherence, and A as a mundane fact that would be stated rather than implied. D also fits the unit's evident quarrel over what degraded the service. About 65%. I could not infer when the relief boat went, how many departures were lost, or who in the text makes this point.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: textbook hedge-wins pattern - A ('considers the question settled') and C ('cannot support at all') are the two absolutized poles and fall on form, leaving the calibrated middle.
ENTAILMENT: the stem presupposes the writer holds an attitude towards Cattermay's argument, which deprecates D ('keeps his own judgement off the page').
justification: B is reachable with no passage at all: reject both extremes, reject the no-stance option on the stem's presupposition, take the partial-acceptance option. 'Accepts her numbers but not the cause she assigns them' is additionally the exact shape of the quarrel the other four stems describe. About 75-80%, and unlike q1 this lever needs no domain knowledge - it is the single most-taught test-wise heuristic. I could not infer what Cattermay's numbers are or what cause she assigns them.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: classic main-idea scope triage - A is too narrow (one ramp), B is too broad ('across the country'), C is off-topic ('ticket data', where the unit is plainly about punctuality and timetabling), leaving exactly one right-scope option.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: D is the only option written as a summary - a tricolon, 'a rising X, a slower Y, and a quarrel over what connects them' - rather than as a claim; the register difference alone marks it.
justification: D is essentially free without the passage, and worse, it restates the argument structure that q1-q4 already establish, so within the unit it doubles as an answer key for the other questions. About 90%. I could not infer the setting, the period, or which side the text ultimately favours.

Four near-synonyms for 'fast' (hasty / rapid / swift / brisk) with no stem text whatsoever - the prompt is a bare 'Gap (1)'. 'hasty' carries negative prosody and is the semantic odd-one-out, but that cuts both ways: it is equally likely to be the key (if the context disapproves) or the throwaway. No collocational tell is available without the sentence frame. Chance. Picked B as the highest-frequency neutral default, which is a guess and not an inference.

The lie/lay paradigm, presented symmetrically: base intransitive (lie), its past participle (lain), the transitive past/participle (laid), and the ambiguous form (lay). Each is correct in some syntactic frame, and the option set does not advertise which frame the gap sits in - no visible auxiliary, no infinitive marker, no object. This is a well-built grammar gap. Chance; picked D because past-tense 'lay' is the most commonly keyed member of this paradigm, which is a base rate, not a channel.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: 'In principle' and 'In practice' form a bound antonymic dyad - the canonical 'in principle ... in practice' collocation - while 'In return' and 'In advance' are unrelated fillers that could not occupy a contrastive discourse slot. The dyad advertises that the key is one of its two members, taking the item from 25% to 50% on shape alone.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: within the dyad 'In practice' is the more frequently keyed marker, since keying 'In principle' would oblige the passage to carry an explicit counterpart clause later.
justification: The strongest single finding in the cloze. Two of the four options are a recognisable idiomatic pair and the other two do not compete for the same slot, so a test-wise student halves the item on form and then leans to C on discourse frequency. About 55-60% on C. I never saw the sentence, so the direction of the contrast is a genre judgement. Fix: replace 'In return' and 'In advance' with markers that could actually fill a contrastive slot (e.g. 'In fact', 'By contrast', 'In short') so the dyad stops standing out.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: the set splits 2+2 on an admit/assert axis, and 'concedes' / 'confesses' are near-substitutable in most frames. A test-wise student applies the twin-cancellation heuristic - two options that would both be defensible cannot be the key - and moves to 'boasts' / 'volunteers'.
justification: A real channel that misfires: the cancellation heuristic points away from what I believe is the key. In an argumentative text 'concedes' is the highest-prior speech-act verb and the item is most likely testing concede-versus-confess precision, so a student running the heuristic would be sent into the wrong half of the set. Flagged rather than killed exactly because the channel exists but lands on a distractor. About 35-40% on A. I could not see who is speaking or what is being admitted.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: 3-1 polarity split - 'widely', 'routinely' and 'heavily' are extensive/intensifying adverbs while 'barely' is a minimiser. One option is conspicuously different in kind, which is itself a design tell.
justification: The odd-one-out is salient but the pull is ambidirectional: 'barely' is either the key (the sentence makes a negative point) or the throwaway, and I cannot tell which without the frame. Among the three intensifiers there is no collocational basis to choose, since they take different heads. Picked D on the reasoning that a minimiser is usually only placed in a set when the slot plausibly takes one - weak. About 30-35%. Fix: make all four the same polarity, or make all four collocationally live for the same head.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: A and D are direct contradictories on one proposition - the extra mesh size did / did not release small round fish - which advertises that the key is one of the two and halves the item on shape alone.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: diamond mesh closing under tow, so that nominal mesh size does not translate into an escape opening for a round-bodied fish, is the canonical gear-selectivity fact, and it is option D verbatim. Option C names the canonical remedy (a square-mesh panel), which corroborates the diagnosis rather than competing with it.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: A's 'did what he expected' is narratively implausible as a keyed finding - texts about gear trials get written because something did not work as expected.
justification: Three independent levers converge on D and I am confident with no passage. The A/D contradictory pair alone puts any student at 50%; the fisheries fact is specialist and would help only a minority of Swedish test-takers; but the narrative-shape lever ('as expected' is never the story) is generally available. About 80-85%. I could not infer the vessel, the mesh sizes tried, or what proportion of fish escaped.

The best-built single question in the batch. The four options test four genuinely different propositions - duration overhang, cause of re-binding, who placed the boys, and premium cost - so nothing is eliminable by contradiction or by shared dimension. No absolutizers, matched length and register, and no world-knowledge fact decides it: master attrition, placement by town families, and varying premiums are all historically ordinary. My only lever is a genre convention (a 'What is suggested' stem tends to key the inference-shaped option, here A, which requires comparing two dates), and that is an item-analyst's habit rather than a channel in the item. Picked A at barely above chance. Deliberately not flagged, so that the flag category keeps its meaning against the real channels elsewhere in this batch.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: B and C are contradictories on a single dimension (the channel has the same fall as the ground / a weaker fall than the ground), while A and D are off-dimension fillers. The dyad hands the student a 50% item on shape alone.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: the head race in meadow irrigation must fall more gently than the natural slope so that it gains height relative to the ground along its length and spills out over the meadow. Matching the ground's gradient would never overflow, and running straight downhill would scour. This decides C.
justification: A clean blind solve. The B/C dyad is the student-available lever and is on its own a serious leak; the hydraulic principle then picks C over B for anyone who holds it. About 85%. I could not infer the length of the channel, the terrain, the period, or who built it.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: C is B with the causal arrow reversed (B: oxygen drives decomposition, which releases nutrients; C: released nutrients make the water oxygen-rich, which drives decomposition). A mirrored-causality twin is only ever constructed around a true forward direction, so its presence advertises B as the key.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: oxygen-bearing running water accelerating mineralisation of peat and releasing nutrients is the standard agronomic account of why flood irrigation raised bog-meadow yields - option B verbatim. A asserts the opposite mechanism (preservation) and D names river warping, a different system.
justification: The reversed-causality pair is the strongest structural tell in the LAS half of the batch. C is not a plausible mechanism at all - nutrients do not oxygenate water - so it exists only as B's mirror, and a student who notices that takes B without the passage. Combined with the standard agronomy this is a blind solve. About 85%. I could not infer the yield figures, the years, or the location.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: the stem's own noun eliminates A - an 'överenskommelse' between parties is by definition not a häradsrätt ruling, so the option is wrong on the stem's wording alone.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: a private agreement among farms sharing one stream canonically allocates water in turns, which is option D; D is also the only surviving option that concerns water at all, in a question about a water agreement.
justification: Reached D but not cleanly. Option C (days' labour owed for the digging) is a genuinely ordinary content of such an agreement and I cannot exclude it, and B (shares of the bog hay) is a plausible clause too. About 65-70% on D - a real channel that does not reach the key with confidence. I could not infer the parties, the actual terms, or whether the agreement held.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: hedge-wins triage. B ('är avgjord', settled in Nolvide's favour) and D ('saknar betydelse', of no significance) are the two absolutized poles and fall on form - a scholarly disagreement reported in an expository text is essentially never presented as settled or as unimportant.

ENTAILMENT: the stem asks what conclusion one 'kan ... dra' - a tentative inference - and C is the only option whose own modality matches, carrying 'sannolikt'. Modality matching between stem and key is a recurring giveaway.
justification: C is reachable with no passage: drop both extremes, then prefer the hedged option over A on stem-modality match. Between the two survivors, A ('which source material can settle it') and C ('they have read the same material differently'), C is also much the more common key shape for this question type. About 75%. I could not infer what Pärlhage and Nolvide actually claim, or what the vallar and the kartor show.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: A and B are near-entailing - a grant scaled to the number of residents along the road just is a roughly equal amount per household - so a test-wise student cancels both, since neither can be the key while the other stays defensible.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: D is off-dimension. Three options describe how much the grant was; D describes who it was paid to, which marks it as the throwaway.
PAIR_STRUCTURE: q2's option A presupposes 'även om bidraget fördelades ojämnt' - that the grant WAS distributed unevenly - which contradicts both A and B here and confirms C. See the pair line.
justification: Standalone, twin-cancellation plus the off-dimension throwaway leave C at roughly 60%. With q2's option set visible - and a student always sees it - the presupposed unevenness in q2/A settles it at about 78%. Reported as flag on its own channels; the pair line carries the escalation to kill. I could not infer the actual amounts, the number of households on either road, or when the grant was abolished.

findings: ENTAILMENT: the stem asks for the author's view of the decision, and D expresses no view of the decision at all - it proposes who should pay for a turning area - so it is eliminable on stem-fit.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: A is the only concessive option ('även om ...'), and a conceded point plus a sustained objection is the standard key shape for an author's-stance question in a debate piece.
justification: Honest limit: I cannot separate A from B. The genre prior says people write in when a grant is cut, favouring the anti-decision options A and C, and A's concessive shape favours it over C. But the unevenness that q1 establishes is precisely the fairness argument a defender of the cut would deploy, which keeps B live, and the fact that both B and D touch the vändplan suggests it matters in the text. Roughly A 40 / B 30 / C 20 / D 10. Above chance, not a solve.

findings: RULE 15 / PAIR_STRUCTURE: one-way leak, q2 into q1. The subordinate clause in q2's option A, 'även om bidraget fördelades ojämnt', asserts as settled background exactly the proposition q1 is testing. It contradicts q1/A (scaled to residents, therefore even) and q1/B (roughly equal per household), and confirms q1/C (one road got three times another). A distractor's presupposition hands over the detail question's key.

RULE 15: the reverse direction is weak and ambiguous. Knowing the grant was uneven does not settle q2, because unevenness is rhetorically available to both sides - it is the defender's justification for abolishing the grant (B) and the opponent's conceded point (A). If anything it slightly raises B.

RULE 15: joint solvability - q1 rises from about 60% standalone to about 78% with q2's options in view, while q2 stays near 40%. Both-correct is about 31% against 6.25% for chance, a 5x lift; but the entire lift sits in q1, which crosses the kill line.
justification: Same mechanism as batch19's las-b19-003, in a milder and narrower form: the stance question's option set smuggles in the factual premise that the detail question is testing. It differs from batch19 in being asymmetric - there the two questions propped each other up and the joint rate exceeded both singles, whereas here q2 gives q1 away and gets nothing back. The exposure is therefore concentrated, and so is the repair: strip or replace the concessive clause in q2/A so that it no longer names how the grant was distributed - concede something not tested elsewhere, such as a strained municipal budget. With that clause gone q1 falls back to about 60%, at which point a second, smaller repair applies: rewrite q1/A or q1/B so the two stop mutually entailing. Pair verdict kill, driven entirely by q1.

findings: ENTAILMENT: the stem says 'vid jämförelsen', so the finding is by construction comparative, and C is the only option stating a between-copy variation ('olika färg även på likadana vyer'). A, B and D all describe uniform practice that a single card would show, and no comparison would be needed to establish them.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: A's 'bara' is an absolutizer, and D's 'i de flesta fall' is a frequency claim rather than a comparative finding.
justification: The stem announces the shape of its own answer. Once you notice that a comparison must yield a comparative result, C is the only option in the running - no passage and no domain knowledge required, so this is a student-available lever rather than a specialist one. About 75-80%. I could not infer how many cards were compared, which colours were used, or what the comparison was undertaken for. Fix: neutralise the stem (e.g. 'Vad sägs om hur himlen färglades?') and give A, B and D comparative form as well, so that comparativeness stops selecting the key.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: B is self-defeating and eliminable on logic alone - if the motif were remade for every new edition, a postmark would date the picture closely, which is the opposite of what the stem asks support for. That reduces the field to three.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: among the survivors, D is the most direct and most general answer to 'when the picture was taken', while C only adds shop-shelf lag after printing and A is a contingent fact about one publisher.
justification: A real channel that does not reach the key reliably: after eliminating B I sit at roughly D 50 / C 30 / A 20. C is genuinely defensible on the stem's wording, which is a distractor-quality concern in its own right - C and D are overlapping mechanisms, both amounting to the card outliving the photographic moment, and both may be arguable. Worth passing to the distractor gate. I could not infer the publisher, the town, or the date range involved.

findings: RULE 15 / PAIR_STRUCTURE: mutual reinforcement through a shared premise, not batch19's hypothesis-space enumeration. Both option sets are drawn from one small factual world - a single motif printed and reprinted in editions over many years and hand-coloured each time - so members of each set vouch for members of the other.

RULE 15: q2's option D ('samma motiv kunde tryckas i nya upplagor i många år') supplies precisely the premise that makes q1's option C possible, since 'likadana vyer' to compare exist only if the motif was reprinted. Conversely, taking C in q1 corroborates D in q2 as true background and lifts it above C and A.

RULE 15: joint solvability - q1 about 80% (already a standalone kill on the stem entailment), q2 lifted from about 50% to about 62% by the corroboration. Both-correct about 50% against 6.25% for chance, an 8x lift, higher than las-b20-002's 5x though less concentrated.
justification: A genuine RULE 15 hit, but structurally different from batch19's las-b19-003. There, one question enumerated the hypothesis space and the other's stances inherited it. Here neither question enumerates anything; instead both option sets are written out of the same handful of facts, so a student who assembles the story - one motif, many editions across years, hand-colouring varying between them, therefore a postmark cannot date the photograph - picks C and D together without reading a line of the passage. Answering either question does shift the odds on the other, symmetrically, which is the diagnostic difference from las-b20-002's one-way leak. The remedy is not to break a single clause but to widen the factual base the two option sets draw on, so that the wrong options in each set are not merely false but unrelated to the other question's subject matter. Pair verdict flag: q1 is independently a kill on its own stem, and the pair effect adds a real but secondary lift to q2.
